acceptance_criteria: BusyPeriod type added. cargo test -p jmap-calendars-types exits 0.
description:
**What:** Add BusyPeriod struct to crate-jmap-calendars-types. Draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §2.2 defines BusyPeriod as a named data object returned by Principal/getAvailability. Fields: utcStart (String/UTCDateTime), utcEnd (String/UTCDateTime), busyStatus (Option<String> — "confirmed"|"tentative"|"unavailable"), event (Option<CalendarEvent>), accountId (Option<Id>).

**Algorithm:**
1. Add to capability.rs or a new availability.rs module:
   #[non_exhaustive]
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
   pub struct BusyPeriod {
       pub utc_start: String,
       pub utc_end: String,
       #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
       pub busy_status: Option<String>,
       #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
       pub event: Option<crate::CalendarEvent>,
       #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
       pub account_id: Option<jmap_types::Id>,
   }
2. Re-export from lib.rs.
3. Add round-trip serde test using a JSON fixture with all fields from spec §2.2 field definitions (hand-written, not derived from code).
4. Run cargo test -p jmap-calendars-types.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- BusyPeriod publicly accessible from crate root.
- Wire names: utcStart, utcEnd, busyStatus, event, accountId.
- cargo test -p jmap-calendars-types exits 0. Clippy clean.
title: Add BusyPeriod struct (Principal/getAvailability response object §2.2)
